chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about the daytime supererogatory prayer. He said:

"Sixteen rakʿahs, whenever you are energetic. Indeed, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام had periods during the day in which he would perform them; then if an estate or the ruler occupied him, he would make them up. The supererogatory prayer is only like a gift: whenever it is brought, it is accepted."

key_terms.الْهَدِيَّةِ: a gift, used here as a comparison for voluntary devotion
key_terms.سَاعَاتٌ مِنَ النَّهَارِ: periods of the daytime allocated for prayer
key_terms.سِتَّ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً: sixteen units of prayer prescribed here for the daytime nafilah
key_terms.قَضَاهَا: he made them up after missing their time
key_terms.مَتَى مَا نَشِطْتَ: whenever you are energetic or able

ai.seo_question: How many rakʿahs are in the daytime nafilah, and can they be made up later?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the daytime nafilah consists of sixteen rakʿahs and may be performed whenever one has the energy for it. It also presents the practice of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام, who would make it up if worldly responsibilities delayed him, and likens nafilah to a gift that is accepted whenever it is offered.
